messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High kv-cache miss/eviction rate detected in us-east-1-a (service: continuous-batcher). Error rate spike -> 5xxs + p99 latency. Pager: https://pager.redwood/incident/2065012345 :rotating_light:
oncall-ryan: i'm on it, grabbing logs and recent deploy diffs. any customer-facing symptoms yet?
maya: seeing a correlated deploy ~15m ago: 
```
  deploy: batching-config-2026-03-15
  changes:
    batch.max_wait_ms: 40 -> 120
    batch.max_tokens: 256 -> 512
    kv_cache.allow_structured: false -> true
```
this toggled structured output caching for funcalls. suspecting key explosion from large JSON responses.
raj: logs show eviction storm + huge key churn. snippet: `cache_evictions=4721 keys_added=5302 avg_key_len=1.2k entries_per_key=1` and this repeated across shards. also seeing `funcall_response_size` spikes to > 120k tokens for some tool results.
oncall-ryan: ok — two-pronged attack: 1) stop caching structured funcall outputs 2) temporarily tighten batch windows. i'll push config rollback for `kv_cache.allow_structured` and reduce `batch.max_wait_ms`.
maya: can we also short-circuit toolcall prefetches? some callers were prefetching whole arrays which blow up the KV index.
raj: yes, we can add a quick rule: `toolcall.prefetch_size_limit=1024` and drop `prefetch=true` for routes that return arrays.
oncall-ryan: executing hotfix now. running command: 
```
redwoodctl config set continuous-batcher.batch.max_wait_ms=50 --env=prod --region=us-east-1-a
redwoodctl config set kv_cache.allow_structured=false --env=prod --region=us-east-1-a
redwoodctl config set toolcall.prefetch_size_limit=1024 --env=prod --region=us-east-1-a
```
please watch for deploy-bot events.
deploy-bot: started rollout of config changes (target: us-east-1-a). 3 nodes at a time.
maya: adding a temporary circuit-breaker to drop toolcall caching entirely if eviction_rate > 10%: `kv_cache.circuit_breaker.eviction_pct=10`
raj: noted. also routing some heavy routes to model-variant `gpt-medium-compact` to reduce token churn. command: `routing set /api/v1/funcall model_variant=gpt-medium-compact region=us-east-1-a`
emily-cs: which customers are seeing errors? need a short blast if any paying tenants impacted.
oncall-ryan: looks like prod-tenant-42 and analytics-proxy saw retries and 502s starting 10:32 UTC. impact: intermittent errors and elevated latency for ~12 minutes pre-hotfix. will get a list from logs and estimate RPS affected.
sarah: taking over oncall for the next hour. ryan — can you paste the query to pull affected customers? i'll reach out to CS for comms.
oncall-ryan: query: `SELECT tenant, count(*) as err FROM request_logs WHERE service='continuous-batcher' AND status>=500 AND ts BETWEEN 1678889500 AND 1678890100 GROUP BY tenant;` returns prod-tenant-42 (460 errs), analytics-proxy (120 errs), internal-infra (30 errs).
emily-cs: thanks. i'll draft a short notification: "We observed intermittent 5xxs impacting specific API routes between 10:32-10:48 UTC. Root cause: KV cache eviction storm triggered by structured funcall outputs and a recent batch config change. Hotfix deployed; systems stabilizing."
sarah: metrics are trending down. p50/p95 back to normal, p99 dropping from 1.8s -> 320ms. eviction rate graph attached. :thumbsup:
raj: followup action items: 1) revert structured caching until we have safe key normalization for JSON arrays 2) add server-side guard limiting cache key cardinality per-request 3) add canary gating for batch config changes 4) postmortem with replay of offending toolcall payloads.
oncall-ryan: logging the incident in incidents tracker and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem.
deploy-bot: rollout complete in us-east-1-a (status: success).
emily-cs: customers notified. no escalations so far.
maya: quick note — we should add a test harness that generates mixed structured tool outputs to exercise KV key cardinality. i can put together a bench.
sarah: agreed. setting action items and owners: maya -> bench + test, raj -> key-normalization design, eng-sre -> canary gating policy.
oncall-ryan: thanks everyone — handing off to sarah for monitoring and postmortem followup.
sarah: i'll take this through to a full postmortem. adding timeline, impact table, and next-steps. if anything flares i'll re-alert. :white_check_mark:
